perQuery.note: A surfaces both landmarks (PARTNER 3 at #1, Evolut 6-year at #2) whereas B omits PARTNER 3 and leads with a meta-analysis.
Both return the exact DAPA-HF paper at #1, but B's remaining results are relevant high-quality follow-ups while A is padded with reviews and a correction notice.
Both lead with CLARITY-AD; B adds more 2026 real-world evidence (recency-favored) but drifts to tangential neuroinflammation/non-cognitive items, while A includes a junk 'Developing Topics' entry.
A stays on PICO with SGLT2i CV-outcome meta-analyses in T2DM, whereas B drifts to kidney/CKD outcomes and includes off-target HF and semaglutide items.
B ranks the 2016/2020/current-2024 ESC AF guidelines more cleanly, while A buries the 2024 update at #9 as a translation and repeats many 2016 duplicates.
A is dominated by on-target DOAC-vs-warfarin network meta-analyses, whereas B is cluttered with device-surgery, Watchman, CKD and diabetes-subgroup tangents.
A leads with the canonical NEJM RECOVERY dexamethasone paper and keeps the medRxiv preprint in scope, while B is heavy with journal-club commentary and secondary write-ups.
Both return the KEYNOTE-189 primary paper at #1, but A's supporting list is cleaner whereas B includes an unidentified entry and an off-target KEYNOTE-021 cohort.
A resolves the acronym to the primary NEJM DAPA-HF results paper plus relevant substudies, while B omits the primary results paper and leads with commentaries.
A contains the PARTNER 3 NEJM landmark plus 5/7-year follow-ups (despite IPV/care-planning noise), whereas B is almost entirely the unrelated HIV PARTNER study and misses the TAVR trial.
A maps the acronym to KEYNOTE-189 (primary at #10 plus updated/5-year analyses), while B misses the NEJM primary and pulls in unrelated KEYNOTE-590/859/789/495 trials.
B includes both the original 2015 SPRINT RCT and the 2021 final report, whereas A returns the final report but omits the original landmark trial.
A gives a coherent set of HFrEF management reviews, while B mixes useful items (DIAMOND, HFA consensus) with off-target hemodialysis and AF papers.
A surfaces the authoritative 2019 ATS/IDSA guideline and the NEJM antibiotic-strategy RCT, whereas B is dominated by older AFP reviews and non-English guidance with several missing IDs.
A includes landmark DOAC RCTs (ROCKET-AF, ARISTOTLE) and key trials, while B returns only older reviews and seminars with no landmark anticoagulation trials.
Both return ProCESS/ARISE/ProMISe and their meta-analysis, but B ranks the strongest pooled evidence (ARISE/ProCESS/ProMISe SR and the patient-level NEJM meta) at the very top.
A leads with Oxygen-ICU and the pivotal IOTA meta-analysis cleanly, whereas B ranks lower-quality items and includes an off-target TRICC transfusion trial.
B anchors on the SELECT CV-outcomes trial plus newer SURMOUNT-5 analyses, while A omits the key SELECT primary and drifts to weight-loss and cost commentary.
Neither retrieves the pivotal KarMMa/CARTITUDE trials; A stays focused on myeloma CAR-T reviews while B is newer but drifts to lymphoma, CAR-NK and microRNA topics.
A leads with high-quality network/pairwise meta-analyses and the Cochrane review, whereas B mixes in older and weaker reviews and an opinion piece.
A ranks the canonical 5-trial Lancet 2022 SGLT2i meta-analysis and EMPEROR/DAPA pooled analysis at the top, while B's meta-analyses are solid but lower-impact.
Both return strong steroid-sepsis SRs, but B surfaces three Cochrane review versions (the query's explicit target) plus the JAMA-IM meta-analysis higher up.
B ranks the current 2020 ACC/AHA VHD guideline and 2017 focused update higher, while A repeats the 2014 guideline (including a malformed-PMID duplicate) and buries 2020.
A cleanly returns both the KDIGO 2024 executive and full CKD guideline at #2/#3, whereas B's #1 is correct but #2-#3 are the wrong KDIGO guidelines (transplant, ADPKD).
A includes the landmark long-term RCT data (STAMPEDE 5-year NEJM, Mingrone Lancet 5-year) plus the JAMA 2024 outcomes, while B is dominated by older SRs and misses the pivotal RCTs.
Both surface the key long-term left-main evidence; A leads with the IPD meta-analysis and SYNTAX/PRECOMBAT 10-year data while B leads with EXCEL 10-year and 5-year outcomes.
B returns the primary DAPA-CKD NEJM trial at #1 plus follow-ups, whereas A includes prespecified analyses and baseline papers but omits the primary results paper.
Both return strong population cohorts and SRs quantifying post-mRNA myocarditis; B edges ahead with broader population data and the pivotal Israeli BNT162b2 NEJM study.
B offers a cleaner mix of cohort, case-control and meta-analytic pancreatitis evidence, while A is diluted by several conference-abstract entries.
Both cover DKA-risk evidence well, but B includes a completely irrelevant pembrolizumab urothelial-carcinoma entry with a malformed PMID, hurting its trust.

overall.summary: Engine A won 17 queries, Engine B 10, with 3 ties. A was more consistent on landmark recall for acronym and long-term-outcome queries (PARTNER 3, KEYNOTE-189, DAPA-HF, bariatric RCTs) and kept top-10 lists tightly on-target, while B repeatedly omitted primary landmark papers or drifted to adjacent topics. B's strengths were recency-sensitive and exact-paper queries (DAPA-HF exact, SPRINT original+final, SELECT, DAPA-CKD primary) where it retrieved the key trial that A missed.
